scope: single organization per deployment; multiple projects/users; no shared-customer hosting

epics.title: [D2] B02 · Immutable run manifests and admission pins
epics.decision: Resolve every pin, including policy and any enabled rule bundle, before the first manifest insert. Never fill pins in an existing manifest. Store immutable canonical bytes and digest; one manifest per run. PostgreSQL database constraints/triggers plus runtime-role privileges must reject UPDATE/DELETE, including bulk SQL; mirror declared development semantics in SQLite. Canonical admission intent contains requested release selector, workflow, input, purpose and server-derived scope, not the selector's current resolved value. On retry authorize first, then return the original manifest for equal intent even if aliases moved; changed intent is 409. New contracts carry fixed deployment organization, project, region and residency; reject caller organization switching. Legacy runs remain explicitly legacy and cannot fabricate historical pins. Allocate a fresh migration revision at implementation time.

epics.title: [D2] B03 · Subject/workload identity, grants and policy decisions
epics.decision: Subject and workload are distinct typed principals. Grants bind run_id, grant_id, subject, workload, project, allowed actions/resources, expiry and policy version; no newest-grant or ambient fallback. Use explicit action/risk maps, never lexical ordering. Resolve admission policy before immutable manifest creation. Recheck current membership, revocation, expiry and resource scope before resume/dispatch; deny on unavailable authority. Record decisions separately, using the existing audit.record API. Beta keeps a human accountable owner and human protected-action approval; it does not expose L3-L5.

epics.title: [D3] B04 · Protected-effect dispatcher (part 2 of 2, 3 of 4 PW)
epics.decision: The public dispatcher is the sole supported effect boundary; unintegrated paths fail closed. No temporary approval hook returning True. Submission may persist a proposed action without dispatch; dispatch waits for exact-intent approval validation, policy and captured owner lease. The dispatcher calls a private raw connector transport, not public OpenAPI execution recursively. Retain D1 prototype tests as historical fixtures, not production implementations. Every inventory entry is routed or refused, including reads requiring authorization, unknown MCP tools and model tool loops.

epics.title: [D3] B05 · Logical effect ledger and verified receipts (part 2 of 2, 3 of 4 PW)
epics.decision: Use ADR 0003 seven states proposed/approved/dispatched/committed/failed/unknown/reconciled. Logical identity is (deployment, run, node, durable occurrence_id); retries reuse it, legitimate loop iterations do not. Separate immutable intent digest covers arguments, target/version and connector version; conflicting intent on one key returns 409. A policy-approved read still records approved before dispatched. Verify receipts against key, intent, target and expected version. A timeout, ConnectionError after possible send, or missing lookup is unknown unless connector evidence proves final non-commit. Recover abandoned dispatched attempts as well as unknown. A 404 or precondition support alone never proves no late commit. Preserve original If-Match and actual emitted idempotency key; retries need known key scope, retention and conflict semantics. Keep legacy in_progress visible in a segregated reconciliation path. Captured owner/token/expiry must match inside the transaction; stale workers cannot record new transitions.

epics.title: [D3] B06 · Exact-intent approvals
epics.decision: Bind proposal digest, evidence, target/version, policy, approver identity and expiry. The approval HTTP endpoint records a decision, not consumption. Consume the decision and claim dispatch atomically in the dispatch transaction with current authorization and owner fence; remote commit is outside that transaction. Changed intent/version supersedes approval. Concurrent retries consume at most once and leave recoverable dispatched state. Beta distinct editor/reviewer/approver checks use authorized human principals and preserve existing quorum rules.

epics.title: [D2] B07 · Authorized context manifest and rule bundle (part 1 of 2, 3 of 4 PW)
epics.decision: Authorize before source bytes are loaded; no reference-profile pass-through. Use current project primary-key type and principal contracts from B03. A context manifest is immutable, ordered, digest-bound, with instruction/data trust labels, source/version/transform/retrieval provenance, omitted/redacted items and token allocation. Register new v1 schemas in contracts.registry; do not use schema_version="1". Add later fields readers-first. Foreign-scope failures expose no source identifiers or payload.

epics.title: [D3] B07 · Authorized context manifest and rule bundle (part 2 of 2, 1 of 4 PW)
epics.decision: Rule bundles are operator-authored, validated, digest-pinned at initial admission and read from verified immutable bytes. Context attachments cannot mutate an existing RunManifest. Allocation/omission records describe the actual consumed context; untrusted source text never becomes policy.

epics.title: [D3] B08 · Bounded typed AgentStep and adapter conformance
epics.decision: AgentStepAdapter returns typed proposed actions, never invokes protected tools itself. Use schema_version=v1 and a single ProposedAction contract shared with B04/B05; use arguments/target consistently. Record node and durable occurrence identity. The platform enforces max_turns, max_tool_calls, max_tokens and deadline before work and after returned usage. Atomically reserve tokens; retries cannot release an uncertain call's reservation or double-charge settlement. M08 extends this ledger rather than inventing a parallel budget authority. Five existing WorkflowExecutor adapters need individual regression coverage.

epics.title: [D4] B09 · Deterministic acceptance and side-effect-free replay
epics.decision: Acceptance is an authoritative domain predicate, not HTTP success or model text. Idempotent decision identity includes run, candidate, criteria version and observation digest. Preserve public run-state compatibility: inspect transition consumers and introduce explicit acceptance outcome without silently relabeling legacy completed runs. Store observation bytes with StorageBackend, not the prompt ArtifactStore; index by durable occurrence and request digest. Historical replay is read-only (including original SQL state), with provider/effect spies proving zero calls. Bounded synchronous replay returns 200 with its report. Counterfactual execution is a new authorized/budgeted run with isolated state; deterministic adapters by default, no protected writes.

epics.title: [D4] B10 · Workspace evaluation execution and release eligibility
epics.decision: Reuse claim_workspace_release_evaluation, heartbeat and complete methods; do not create a second queue. Resolve the release's own pinned dataset/judge/config, not an unrelated run manifest. Mark simulated versus real evaluation explicitly. Lease loss permits multiple external attempts, but only one authoritative fenced completion; retain orphan-attempt provenance and deduplicate association, not an impossible exactly-one MLflow-run promise. Hard acceptance/security failures cannot be bypassed by break-glass. Disabled feature remains 404; enabled but unavailable adapter is structured 409.

epics.title: [D2] B11 · Trace ownership and run correlation (part 2 of 3, 1 of 2.5 PW)
epics.decision: Canonical experiment identity is (configured tracking backend, resolved numeric experiment ID), not raw name/ID strings. Claim/read/create/update must resolve identically; failure is deny, not fallback. One atomic owner registry covers agent and workflow claims. New claims require server-controlled provenance; arbitrary pre-existing experiment IDs cannot be appropriated. Legacy conflicting claims are quarantined for explicit operator resolution, never last-writer-wins. Redaction and payload permission checks precede fetching payload, consistently for detail/list/search/metrics/export.

epics.title: [D3] B11 · Trace ownership and run correlation (part 3 of 3, 0.5 of 2.5 PW)
epics.decision: Causal links reference actual persisted IDs and expose missing links explicitly. D3 cannot claim an acceptance record before B09 exists in D4; B14 closes the full chain. Add matching typed sync and async SDK behavior and permission-negative tests.

epics.title: [D2] B12 · Reference deployment profile and refusals (part 2 of 4, 0.5 of 2.5 PW)
epics.decision: Extend the existing nine startup refusals and readiness checks, do not recreate them. Bound streamed request bodies even without Content-Length. Strict profile refuses unowned/free-form memory until server-derived ownership and M20 lifecycle exist. Secret canaries must remain absent from traces, errors, exports and logs. PostgreSQL 16 + pgvector is the Beta reference profile; SQLite is development-only.

epics.title: [D3] B12 · Reference deployment profile and refusals (part 3 of 4, 0.5 of 2.5 PW)
epics.decision: Trusted connector admission binds registered implementation/configuration digest and effect capabilities, never a caller-supplied tool name. A custom tool called document_request is not trusted. Refuse arbitrary MCP stdio/remote hosts, host-file exports and PostgreSQL MCP writes in the Beta reference profile until their exact dispatcher contracts are supported.

epics.title: [D4] B12 · Reference deployment profile and refusals (part 4 of 4, 0.5 of 2.5 PW)
epics.decision: Refuse executable/code node kinds using the compiler's actual kind registry and enforce at compile, promote and execute boundaries. Plugin allowlisting is trusted-code admission, not hostile-code containment. Preserve current CSRF/origin/header protections and test them through public paths.

epics.title: [D2] B13 · Execution-owner lease, fencing and outbox/inbox (part 1 of 2, 2 of 2.5 PW)
epics.decision: Capture Lease(owner_id, fencing_token, expires_at) when acquired. Renew the same ownership token; increment only on a new acquisition. Database time governs expiry. Each transition compares exact owner and token plus unexpired lease inside its transaction, not token < latest or a freshly read current_token. All owner-only loops stop claiming when lease is lost; API-only replicas continue serving safe APIs. SQL outbox is atomic with business transition; delivery is at-least-once with durable acknowledged handoff and consumer deduplication. SSE/in-process fan-out is a notification, not durable business truth. Cover crash before handoff, after handoff before mark, and during consume.

epics.title: [D3] B13 · Execution-owner lease, fencing and outbox/inbox (part 2 of 2, 0.5 of 2.5 PW)
epics.decision: Inbox identity is consumer/source/event-id. Reservation, business transition and processed marker commit together, or hand off to a durable queue before acknowledgement. A failed transaction must be retryable, never incorrectly treated as already processed. Webhook signature and project authorization precede parsing/dispatch. Preserve owner fencing through recovery and keep reconciliation enabled during stops.

epics.title: [D4] B14 · Joined evidence export and verifier (part 1 of 2, 1 of 2.5 PW)
epics.decision: Use v1 registered evidence schema. Join immutable manifest/context/proposal/policy/approval/effect/receipt/acceptance/evaluator provenance and explicit missing-link status. Hash canonical metadata, parent links and complete membership, not only payload digests. Keep raw and authorized redacted views distinct. StorageBackend owns generic evidence bytes.

epics.title: [D5] B14 · Joined evidence export and verifier (part 2 of 2, 1.5 of 2.5 PW)
epics.decision: Redact before hashing the exported view; cache/object key includes view digest and authorization scope. Offline verifier rejects omitted/swapped links, altered metadata and unsafe archive members (traversal, symlink, duplicate name, size/bomb limits) without extractall. Unsigned Beta integrity does not prove origin; M02/M05 add signatures/checkpoints. Reuse a single server-free verification contract across SDK/CLI, with sync/async API parity.

epics.title: [D5] B15 · Synthetic downstream, cookbook and SDK/CLI journey
epics.decision: Reuse the D1 synthetic downstream and existing case fixture. Its POST is 201 first commit, 200 key replay, 412 stale If-Match; do not recreate conflicting routes. Vendor only permitted book fixture material with exact commit/license. One lab 22 identity is reused by M26, not a second conflicting cookbook directory. Show UI/API/SDK/CLI happy path and denial/unknown/replay/export from installed artifacts.

epics.title: [D5] B16 · Public fault matrix and Beta acceptance report (part 2 of 2, 3 of 4 PW)
epics.decision: Keep alpha browser journeys and add Beta coverage; do not replace alpha regressions. All applicable required checks execute; skipped required jobs never count as pass. The milestone control #613 owns D5-acceptance.md; these tasks supply evidence fragments tied to exact SHA/artifact. A restore after an unknown write must prove preserved pins and one external mutation after reconciliation, not equality with a receipt absent at backup time. Separate offline fault proof, bounded real-provider quality evidence and independent human security review.

epics.title: [D6] M01 · Workload identity and credential leases
epics.decision: Workload tokens bind issuer, audience, worker principal, expiry and nonce; use a standard authenticated format and test every claim. Credential leases bind exact run/grant/decision/resource/action, expire and redeem atomically with use counts. Secrets never enter model context or logs. Revoke on cancellation/deprovisioning; broker outage is fail-closed. Deployment bootstrap secret mounts are distinct from connector credential leasing.

epics.title: [D6] M02 · Signed bundles, canary and rollback
epics.decision: Signature is outside the canonical bundle content digest, avoiding self-reference. Verify current registered schema versions, trust key, digest, policy and compatibility before admission. Promotion moves an environment binding to the same evaluated digest, not rebuilt content. Deterministic canary hashing has exact fixture expectations. Quarantine stops new affected dispatch without rewriting pinned history or losing reconciliation for in-flight unknown effects.

epics.title: [D8] M03 · Second connector, partial effects and compensation
epics.decision: Extend the production proposal/effect contract from B05, not the legacy ledger. Introduce a versioned state extension readers-first for partial/intervention_required, with storage widths accommodating names. Legacy records remain compatible. Compensation is a separately authorized proposal linked to the original receipt; never rewrite the original effect as if undone. Redrive requires authoritative outcome evidence and a fresh valid grant; missing lookup alone is not safety.

epics.title: [D7] M04 · Knowledge lifecycle and tombstones
epics.decision: Reuse current knowledge version/release/activation seams; add only missing signed approval/binding/lineage contracts. Existing runs retain pins, but revoked sources are refused at reuse. Deletion immediately removes active retrieval access, invalidates caches and records a durable propagation job/tombstone; archive legal hold never keeps deleted memory or knowledge active.

epics.title: [D6] M05 · Protected audit archive
epics.decision: Archive integrity needs signed chain checkpoints and object version IDs/conditional create. S3 Object Lock does not prevent writing a new version at the same key. Separate runtime append credentials, audit-reader permission and retention-controller credentials. Protect SQL append-only semantics for the runtime role, while stating the DBA threat boundary. Legal hold and retention operate only on retained archive copies; outages retain durable backlog and block required release evidence.

epics.title: [D6] M06 · Approval timers, overrides and scoped stop
epics.decision: Reuse B06 expiry columns and services, never duplicate schema or call route handlers from janitors. Claim/reassign/expire use atomic state transitions. Overrides cannot bypass project scope, exact intent, authoritative receipt or non-waivable critical controls. Scoped stop prevents new authorization; already in-flight remote work still needs reconciliation.

epics.title: [D7] M07 · Isolated worker profile and egress limits
epics.decision: Extend existing ToolSandboxConfig/backend factory. Use network=none and a broker-mediated framed RPC over stdio for explicitly allowed capabilities; do not pretend HTTP_PROXY on a Unix socket works with network=none. No ambient environment, host mounts, Docker socket or raw credentials inside the tool. Wall timeout, CPU quota and cumulative CPU-time limit are distinct controls. Track and remove only containers created by this sandbox instance; never globally remove all labeled containers. Pinned image digest and enforced resource limits are mandatory.

epics.title: [D8] M08 · Persistent budgets, bulkheads and fair queues
epics.decision: Extend B08 reservations with integer micro-USD money and integer token units, transactional capacity checks and unique idempotent settlement. Unknown usage retains a conservative reservation pending reconciliation. Explicit bucket types deployment/project/run/connector avoid fake run foreign keys. One retry authority covers model/read retries; ambiguous effects use B05 reconciliation. Use bounded weighted round-robin within priority with aging after a configured finite wait; test non-starvation deterministically.

epics.title: [D6] M09 · Trajectory evaluation gates and waivers (part 1 of 2, 1 of 3 PW)
epics.decision: Reuse existing judge/version models where present. Gate records pin judge, criteria, dataset and evidence digests. Security/authorization, deterministic acceptance and critical trajectory invariants are non-waivable. Human-owned, scoped, expiring waivers apply only to explicitly enumerated noncritical quality thresholds and are recorded on every use.

epics.title: [D7] M09 · Trajectory evaluation gates and waivers (part 2 of 2, 2 of 3 PW)
epics.decision: Historical replay reproduces recorded observations and cannot establish candidate model quality. Evaluate candidates with pinned deterministic adapters for CI and separately bounded real-provider trials for quality; retain dataset/model/judge/provider provenance. Every critical slice passes regardless of mean improvement. Domain owner approves corpus, thresholds and spending cap before live trial; #608 records that input, not invented success.

epics.title: [D7] M10 · Governed feedback and candidate release (part 1 of 2, 1 of 2.5 PW)
epics.decision: Preserve true feedback creator identity. Do not backfill creator from assignee; legacy unknown creator requires explicit human review before promotion. Accepted feedback creates a new immutable dataset version with trace/source lineage and project authorization.

epics.title: [D9] M10 · Governed feedback and candidate release (part 2 of 2, 1.5 of 2.5 PW)
epics.decision: Split and freeze held-out data before candidate generation, grouping related examples to avoid leakage. Candidate count, tokens, time and spend are bounded. Candidate evaluation does not reuse historical model output as a substitute for execution. Preserve existing calibration/refinement job behavior outside the new governed path. Apply uses current authorization, distinct reviewer and all non-waivable gates.

epics.title: [D7] M11 · Hardened deployment, upgrade and restore (part 1 of 3, 1 of 4 PW)
epics.decision: Extend the existing deployment artifact instead of maintaining a second drifting stack. Pin reference PostgreSQL16/pgvector, MLflow and object-store images. A coordinated backup records SQL, MLflow and object versions in one restore manifest, with bounded quiescence or documented consistency point. Bootstrap secrets do not imply reusable tool credentials.

epics.title: [D8] M11 · Hardened deployment, upgrade and restore (part 2 of 3, 1 of 4 PW)
epics.decision: Preflight requires exclusive migration ownership/quiesced writers, verified compatible backup and storage/DB schema checks. Record exact prior/new revision and artifact digests. Never edit a shipped migration checksum; use a fresh forward migration.

epics.title: [D9] M11 · Hardened deployment, upgrade and restore (part 3 of 3, 2 of 4 PW)
epics.decision: Do not repair old migration 0026 or any shipped migration in place. Define a supported rollback horizon: tested forward-compatible previous binary or restore the certified coordinated backup. Restore verifies SQL, object and MLflow references, immutable manifests, ownership fencing and unknown-effect visibility. Independent operator means a person other than the implementation author, not agent self-attestation.

epics.title: [D9] M12 · Workload envelope, SLOs and recovery drills
epics.decision: Operating limits are measured, not inferred from unit coverage. Run repeated deterministic workloads and retain variation; arbitrary percentage similarity is not a reliable pass oracle. Domain owner approves SLO, cost and recovery targets before pilot. Credentials use environment/file input, never CLI arguments/logs. Offline CI uses synthetic services; provider trials are separately budgeted.

epics.title: [D8] M13 · Durable bounded child task
epics.decision: Child task scope and budget are intersections/reservations from the parent, never a new authority source. Persist child identity and typed result; retry attempts do not create new logical child/effect occurrences. Cancellation blocks new dispatch but cannot recall an in-flight remote commit; retain unknown state and reconciliation. Parent settlement is atomic and avoids double accounting.

epics.title: [D7] M14 · Runtime/connector conformance suite (part 1 of 2, 1 of 2.5 PW)
epics.decision: Conformance targets the actual AgentStepAdapter and connector protocols, using stable semantic projections rather than byte equality of timestamps/UUIDs. Installed wheel fixtures run outside the checkout and required checks cannot skip for missing local files. Unknown capabilities fail closed.

epics.title: [D9] M14 · Runtime/connector conformance suite (part 2 of 2, 1.5 of 2.5 PW)
epics.decision: Follow existing SDK model conventions and sync/async resource surfaces; do not add Pydantic as a new SDK dependency just to mirror server models. Versioned fixtures exercise old/new reader compatibility and declared unsupported versions. Conformance must execute M03/M13 failure semantics, not just signature matching.

epics.title: [D8] M15 · Second use case and independent pilot (part 1 of 2, 1 of 2.5 PW)
epics.decision: Use the same public admission/dispatcher/acceptance contracts as the first use case. Behavioral spies prove no bypass and externally observed results prove domain acceptance; source grep alone is not an architecture test.

epics.title: [D9] M15 · Second use case and independent pilot (part 2 of 2, 1.5 of 2.5 PW)
epics.decision: An independent operator/user must execute the installed-artifact pilot; authors cannot certify their own independence. Core D9 proof is not the full MVP release; clearly separate measured behavior, preview features and retained D10-D15 obligations.

epics.title: [D15] M16 · Independent security review and MVP release decision
epics.decision: Full MVP remains single-tenant, including identity, regional cells, Hub, memory, federation, catalog and autonomy. All applicable required checks must run and pass on exact rebuilt artifacts; no skipped-required-check waiver. Critical/high security findings are resolved before release, not accepted by an author waiver. Residual lower severity findings require explicit independent review. Owner performs final PR review/merge; do not merge automatically.

epics.title: [D3] Separation of duties on prompt/job Apply (child of B06)
epics.decision: Apply separation covers all job creation paths and atomic apply claims. Unknown legacy creator is not automatically allowed in the reference profile: require explicit human review/quarantine. Preserve and document declared legacy development compatibility only. Distinct approver plus current project permission and exact candidate digest are rechecked at apply.

epics.title: [D7] Trace → refinement loop (child of M10 part 1)
epics.decision: Reuse existing trace-to-refinement workflow; add creator/reviewer provenance, project-safe trace selection and immutable dataset lineage without replacing established calibration jobs. Never infer permission from a client-supplied experiment alias.

epics.title: [D5] Beta: upgrade path from the 0.1.0a1 database
epics.decision: Derive the alpha migration head and fixture schema from tag caliber-v0.1.0a1, not an assumed numeric revision. Freeze checksums of shipped migration files. Seed via that tagged schema, upgrade through fresh migrations, preserve counts/payloads and explicitly mark old runs legacy without invented pins. Test both SQLite development and reference PostgreSQL16.

epics.title: [D5] Beta: promote the integrations and release-candidate areas from feature-flagged preview to supported
epics.decision: Promote only capabilities demonstrated by Beta gates for the supported profile/connector. Do not label every integration/MCP backend supported or invent a FeatureFlag stability enum without compatibility checks. UI reads actual capability metadata. Disabled paths retain consistent errors; alpha documentation remains historical.

epics.title: [D11] M17 · Single-tenant enterprise identity and deprovisioning
epics.decision: One server-configured organization per installation, multiple authorized projects/users. No customer tenant router, universal tenant-column retrofit, shared-customer keys/quotas or tenancy certification. Retain required new contract scope fields, dedicated deployment credentials/storage/backup boundaries, OIDC and SCIM. External identity key is issuer+sub, not automatic email linking. OIDC validates issuer/audience/signature/state/nonce/PKCE and safe redirects. SCIM groups map through explicit administrator-approved role bindings, never display-name privilege escalation. Deprovisioning revokes sessions, PATs, project roles, grants, leases and pending approval authority within 60 seconds. V28-identity is required; V28-shared-tenancy is an explicit excluded operating mode, not a passing/skipped test.

epics.title: [D12] M18 · Multi-region execution and residency cells
epics.decision: Regional cells belong to the same organization. Global tier holds signed references/metadata, not resident document payloads. Capture cell region/generation/owner fence; never read latest token to legitimize stale work. Region loss restores into a replacement inside allowed residency and prevents old-cell dispatch; do not copy US-only payloads to EU. RPO/RTO are owner-approved targets and measured outcomes, not promises.

epics.title: [D14] M19 · A2A gateway and federated task adoption
epics.decision: Use one explicitly pinned A2A wire-version adapter with vendored protocol fixtures and license; core contracts stay protocol-neutral. Peer identity, signing keys, scope mapping and allowed origins are administrator-configured. Durable delegation may retry with the same remote idempotency identity; lost acknowledgement is unknown, not proven failure. Callback signatures bind timestamp/body and replay identity; duplicates are idempotent, out-of-order sequence is buffered durably until predecessors arrive. Adoption verifies content hash/schema/signature/residency and local acceptance. Fetching remote artifacts must block SSRF, redirects to forbidden origins and oversized payloads. Remote claims never expand local authority.

epics.title: [D14] M20 · Governed cross-run memory
epics.decision: SQL is authority; mem0 is an optional index behind owned namespaces. Scope derives from authenticated principal/team membership, fixed organization and project, not arbitrary client labels. Writes require recorded consent/purpose, verified provenance, TTL and governed proposal/policy. Use explicit provenance verdicts with instruction/data context labels, not a conflicting numeric trust-tier>=4 scheme. Read rechecks authority, consent and TTL. Correction/deletion invalidates caches/derived links; legal hold retains an inaccessible archive copy, never active retrieval.

epics.title: [D13] M21 · Knowledge Hub: governed extraction, ontology and Hub views
epics.decision: Reuse existing parsers/retrievers through a versioned Extractor protocol; any third-party extraction reuse requires an exact-version/license/domain-corpus comparison before adoption. A span's presence is not proof of its interpreted value: typed field normalization/units/source offsets and independent validators establish verified/contradicted/insufficient verdicts. Ambiguity routes to humans; model assertions cannot self-certify. Base ontology plus organization-specific extensions remain versioned and approved; no shared-tenant CRUD.

epics.title: [D15] M22 · Connector and framework catalog with certification
epics.decision: Catalog trust binds publisher key, certified digest and capability report, never a caliber-* name prefix. Certification runs in isolation, not plugin code in the API process. Revocation blocks new admission and preserves running-effect reconciliation. Independent adapter evidence must come from an independent author; an author-written fallback is not a substitute.

epics.title: [D10] M23 · Routing, ownership transfer and model economics
epics.decision: Use RunManifest.pins.model_routes as the eligible pinned route set, not a second manifest.eligible_routes field. Filter by policy/residency/purpose/risk before ranking cost/latency, tie-break by route ID, fail closed if none. Fallback stays in the pinned set. Task ownership transfer is distinct from the execution-owner lease and cannot duplicate authority before acknowledgement.

epics.title: [D10] M24 · Governance inventory, risk tiers and exceptions
epics.decision: GovernanceRecord owns risk tier, human owner, controls and autonomy level from first schema; M27 extends enforcement, not a competing level store. Critical controls always require pass; domain quality thresholds are versioned configuration approved by owner, not undocumented constants. Reuse M09 waiver control_type and preserve existing values; do not add duplicate columns or retroactively rename release_gate semantics.

epics.title: [D10] M25 · Remaining platform contracts and a second channel
epics.decision: Use versioned contracts and readers-before-writers rollout. Artifact identity is composite (artifact_id,version) or a surrogate version-row key plus unique pair, not artifact_id-only primary key. Include project ownership and fixed organization. Use StorageBackend capability checks for signed URLs; local storage exposes an authorized download route, not a pretend signed URL. Convert event producers before enforcing rejection; support only explicit versioned compatibility during migration. Schema/behavior tests, not broad AST bans on every .publish, prove event correctness. Notifications are durable at-least-once attempts; only an idempotent sink can promise one delivery. Channel ingress requires timestamp-bound signature, replay protection, mapped principal/project and the same admission intent key.

epics.title: [D15] M26 · Companion case and book traceability
epics.decision: Use the existing Beta lab 22, not a second cookbook with the same number. Pin permitted book fixture commit/license; JSON provenance belongs in adjacent metadata, not invalid JSON comments. Traceability checks collect node IDs without recursively running pytest inside pytest; gate runner invokes collected suites once and retains results. V28-shared-tenancy is explicitly excluded, not claimed complete. Cross-repository publication needs an owner-approved book-repository task/PR; absence is visible, never fabricated.

epics.title: [D10] M27 · Autonomy levels: which roles an agent may hold, per use case
epics.decision: Follow ADR0004 exactly: human owner at every level; agent pins differing is necessary evidence, not sufficient independence. Require distinct principals, independent deterministic acceptance and actual current controls. Without verifiable acceptance cap at L2. L4 excludes irreversible/export effects; L5 still intersects explicit policy/legal human-review requirements. GovernanceRecord from M24 owns levels. Agent account provisioning is privileged, not public human signup. Preserve old evidence readers: new principal evidence uses a versioned schema, do not reject all old exports. Promotion requires nonempty adequate decisions AND minimum observation window, one level at a time, no failed critical slice and human owner approval. Defaults 30 days and 200 decisions are conservative targets configurable only by authorized policy. Demotion consumes a deduplicated incident watermark so one incident does not demote repeatedly every 300 seconds; stop higher-autonomy dispatch immediately while reconciliation continues.
